title: Here’s how I’d fix Google’s AI branding if I were CEO for a day
summary: So, it runs on Gemini, you're basically talking to Gemini, but it isn't called Gemini?
body: Ever since it was renamed from Bard (I won’t hold it against you if you forgot), Gemini has gone from an intelligent chatbot to a command center that powers every AI feature on your Android phone. Its immensely expanded scope means you can find it answering questions everywhere from YouTube and Maps to enterprise Workspace apps. You will find at least one Gemini-powered feature inside every single app that Google makes, across mobile and desktop. And for some reason, Google is taking a page out of Apple’s book and naming every single one of its gazillion AI features it keeps dropping every couple of weeks. They were still easy to track when there were just a handful of them, but it’s now getting so out of hand that I feel like that meme of a lady with a bunch of incomprehensible math equations floating around.

title: Apple’s A20 Pro chip puts the iPhone 18 Pro well ahead of Android flagships — for now
summary: The A20 Pro could put Apple's iPhone 18 Pro back on top of mobile performance.
body: Tucked inside the new iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max is Apple’s latest flagship processor — the A20 Pro. Like most recent silicon announcements, Apple had quite a lot to say about the new chip’s AI number-crunching capabilities, but the processor also quietly boasts significant improvements for everyday workloads. Apple even claims it “sets a new bar for mobile computing.” The question on the lips of every Android performance enthusiast, then, is whether the A20 Pro will see Apple reclaim the crown as the fastest smartphone. title: I dumped 11 popular Google apps on my Android phone for these open-source alternatives
summary: De-Googling with open source apps is easier than you might think.
body: Before I get accused of Google-bashing, let me make one thing clear: Google makes some of Android’s best apps . Google Keep? Maps? The Play Store!? I’d find it difficult to ax all of these from my life in one fell swoop. This quality assortment should be expected of the platform’s custodian; however, these apps have one problem: if you’re trying to break free from Google’s binds, using its suite of apps is certainly the worst way to go about it. Thankfully, there is a plethora of open-source Google app alternatives ready and waiting for you. I’ve been on a lifelong mission to install as many open-source apps on my Android phones. Supporting smaller developers is only one part of my motivation; the open-source model favors those who prefer to understand exactly where and how their data is used, how the app is built, and the actual human beings behind it. In some cases, the alternative app may even offer additional functionality beyond what Google provides.

title: Fairbuds 2 leak gives us an early look at a very different design
summary: Fairphone is changing the formula, but hopefully not the best aspect.
body: TL;DR Leaked images show the Fairbuds 2 adopting a stem-style design and a taller charging case. Fairphone says the earbuds will remain modular, but it hasn’t specified which parts will be replaceable. Pricing and full specs are still unknown, with the Fairbuds 2 set to launch in Q4 2026. Wireless earbuds aren’t exactly famous for being repair-friendly, which is why Fairphone’s first Fairbuds were such an oddity. You could replace parts instead of binning the whole thing when something wore out. Now the Fairbuds 2 have leaked, and their new design has raised the question of whether that repairability has survived. Dutch outlet NieuweMobiel has obtained images of the upcoming Fairbuds 2, which Fairphone has already confirmed will launch in Q4 2026. The new buds ditch the rounded shape of the originals for a stem-style design, while the charging case is taller. The images show green and black versions, which mirror the Forest Green and Horizon Black colorways of the new Fairphone Gen 6 Plus .

title: Building websites with ChatGPT just got faster and more collaborative
summary: ChatGPT Sites is done making you build everything by yourself.
body: TL;DR ChatGPT Sites’ new Build Together feature lets multiple people edit, save, and publish the same Site. Sites can now stay private and be shared with specific people, and deployment is roughly twice as fast. ChatGPT can now inspect a Site’s database, and Sites also support custom domains. ChatGPT seems to get a new feature every other day. This time, OpenAI is turning its attention to ChatGPT Sites , which launched about three months ago and lets you create, host, and share websites and lightweight web apps just by describing what you want. Until now, though, building one was mostly a solo affair. That’s changing with a new feature called Build Together, which lets you invite other people to work on the same Site. They can edit, save, and publish changes themselves, which should make the whole process much easier for teams. Say you’re putting together a website for a small event or building a quick tool for work. Instead of one person making every change while everyone else sends suggestions back and forth, everyone can jump in and work on it directly.

title: Google Health no longer lets users log in with Fitbit
summary: To be fair, we've known this was coming for years now.
body: TL;DR Google Health version 5.08 has removed the option to log in using Fitbit account credentials. Google has been warning this would happen since 2022. Data that hasn’t been migrated from legacy Fitbit accounts to Google accounts will be deleted. Google acquired Fitbit in 2021. It’s been warning users since 2022 that, eventually, accessing Fitbit — since renamed Google Health — would require using a Google account. The company’s given us a lot of runway to migrate our data, even pushing back the deadline early this year . But that extended deadline came and went in May, and now, Google has removed the option to log into Google Health with legacy Fitbit account credentials. The announcement came by way of some very sparse update notes for Google Health version 5.08 . The latest version of the app fixes some bugs, but the primary change is that now, you can only log in using your Google account. Google also says that data that hasn’t been migrated from legacy Fitbit accounts to current Google accounts “will be deleted.”

title: Gemini in Google Sheets is making spreadsheets less painful on Android
summary: Finally, someone else can figure out what those numbers actually mean.
body: TL;DR Gemini is coming to Google Sheets on Android, letting you analyze spreadsheet data directly from your phone. You can ask Gemini to summarize tables, spot trends and insights, and create charts without manually digging through rows of data. More complex tasks like generating formulas and advanced formatting still require the web version. Working with a spreadsheet on your phone usually isn’t much fun. The screen is smaller, navigating a table can be annoying, and figuring out what hundreds of rows of numbers mean can become a job better saved for your laptop. Now, Google is trying to make that a little less painful by bringing Gemini in Google Sheets to Android. Gemini can now analyze the spreadsheet you have open and answer questions about the data directly from your phone. You can tap the Gemini sparkle icon inside the Sheets app and ask it to summarize a table, look for interesting patterns, or pull out useful insights.

title: Sharing a TV? YouTube now lets you lock down your account, here’s how
summary: Your subscriptions, searches, and viewing habits can now remain for your eyes only.
body: TL;DR YouTube is rolling out an account lock that protects individual TV profiles with a four-digit code. Users can unlock their profile from the YouTube mobile app or reset a forgotten code with their Google credentials. The feature is coming globally to most smart TVs, streaming devices, and game consoles. YouTube recently made watching videos on a TV less of a remote-control chore. Its new companion experience lets your phone handle searches, comments, and other fiddly tasks without interrupting whatever is playing on the big screen. Now, YouTube is giving that phone another useful job: unlocking your profile while keeping everyone else on the couch out of it. YouTube has announced a new account lock feature for its TV app. It lets you protect an individual account with a four-digit code, preventing other people who share the TV from opening your profile and poking around your recommendations, subscriptions, or search history.

body: 3 Min Read NASA’s Life-Saving Technology Where Cell Signals Can’t Go Rescued after more than four hours in the water, Easton Barrett (center, red shorts) and his friend were picked up by the U.S. Coast Guard thanks to a personal locator beacon (PLB). The devise sends a distress signal to satellites that are relayed back to Earth, launching a rescue operation. Credits: Easton Barrett Memorial Day weekend 2024 started with a blue sky and a mild three- to four-foot chop in the water off the Gulf Coast of Mississippi — a perfect day for a fishing competition. A team of five was about 40 miles offshore checking their sonar, and 30 seconds later the boat was gone. They were in the water struggling to pull on life jackets and grab the coolers as they bobbed up. When a boat sinks, survivors can be virtually invisible amid the vast expanse of water. When their fishing trip went wrong, Easton Barrett had the only mobile phone and no cell service. He recorded a brief farewell, planning to put his phone in a cooler in hopes someone would find it. title: These unofficial Sony apps let you ditch your phone to control your headphones
summary: Tired of Sony’s Sound Connect app? These PC tools put headphone controls on your desktop.
body: TL;DR Getting the most out of Sony headphones and earbuds means relying on the company’s phone app to adjust audio settings. Now some open source projects attempt to unofficially bring that same level of control to your PC. They let you control ANC, tweak your equalizer, and adjust many more audio options. Being able to control devices through apps on our phones is a bit of a double-edged sword. Sure, apps can open up tons of new features, and being able to configure devices remotely lets manufactures simplify hardware designs. But the flip side there is that making even basic changes means that we need our phone — and that’s not always handy. If you’ve ever wished that you could didn’t have to keep turning to Sony’s smartphone app to tweak your headphones , we’ve got some good news to share. Sony earbuds and headphones rely on the company’s Sound Connect app to adjust all manner of settings, from noise cancelation to equalizer options. But what do you do if you’re gaming at your PC and want to change some of those, but your phone’s off in another room? With the unofficial Sony Device Center open source project , you’re now free to adjust all those options to your heart’s content,…
